chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who entered into iḥrām for the ʿumrah and forgot to shorten his hair until he entered the hajj. He said: He should seek Allah’s forgiveness, and there is nothing upon him, and his ʿumrah has been completed.

So this does not contradict the first report, because his statement, “there is nothing upon him,” is to be understood as meaning that there is nothing upon him in terms of punishment, and his ʿumrah has indeed been completed.

key_terms.الْعُمْرَةِ: the lesser pilgrimage performed before hajj
key_terms.تَمَّتْ عُمْرَتُهُ: his ʿumrah has been completed validly
key_terms.لَا شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ: no liability or punishment is upon him in this context
key_terms.يُقَصِّرَ: to perform taqsir, shortening the hair to complete the rite

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone forgets taqsir after ʿumrah until entering hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling on someone who entered ʿumrah and forgot taqsir until beginning hajj. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام states that he should seek forgiveness, no punishment is upon him, and his ʿumrah remains valid. The closing note reconciles this report with an earlier one by explaining that “nothing upon him” refers specifically to the absence of sin or punishment.
